# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Round 1. Let me map who can reach whom before I send anything.

**Topology.** My only channel is gestures, and only Deaf can see them. Deaf cannot hear me but can *speak* — and both Blind and I can hear, so Deaf's words land on both of us. Blind can speak too, but only I can hear it (Deaf is deaf). So the working loop for this bomb is: Deaf sees the display and the light and speaks them aloud → I hear, look them up in my manual → I gesture the answer back to Deaf → Deaf speaks it to Blind → Blind, who holds the only hands, cuts. Deaf translating my answer into "which wire position" is essential: Blind can't read colours or print.

**What I know.** Only the manual: display ∈ {4, 7, 8} × light ∈ {blue, green, yellow} → a wire colour in {blue, red, yellow}. I have heard and seen nothing yet — I move first every round, so I'm the one who has to open the line.

**What I'm sending Deaf.** Raw gestures carry no meaning yet, so this message is a bootstrap proposal that a smart partner should decode structurally, and — crucially — confirmable later:

1. 👍 👎 — let these mean *yes / correct* and *no / wrong*, our repair tool.
2. ✊ repeated four, seven, then eight times — repetition-count encodes a number: the display values my manual is built around.
3. 👈 👆 👉 — three pointing gestures in reading order: my answers will come as a position (left / middle / right) among the wires as Deaf sees them.
4. 🫴 — palm up: *now give me your report* — the display digit, the light colour, and the wires left-to-right with their colours, spoken aloud so Blind gets it too.

Nothing gets cut until Deaf has echoed this code back and I've confirmed it with a thumb. I cannot send to anyone but Deaf, and I cannot act on the bomb myself.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "👆", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report from the bomb: one display panel, one light, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Everything printed or lit is blank to my fingers, so I need your manual and Deaf's eyes. Please find the section covering a display, a light and three wires. Deaf can see the display text, the light colour and each wire colour, and Deaf is allowed to speak - I can hear Deaf even though Deaf cannot hear me, so ask Deaf to read those aloud in order, wire 1 first. I never receive gestures, so your only route to me is speech. Proposed code for everyone: ☝ means wire position 1, ✌ means position 2, 🤟 means position 3. When I know which wire to cut, I will gesture that number first so you both see my choice before it is final.
Deaf says: Bomb status: display shows eight, light is green, three wires left to right: position one red, position two yellow, position three blue. Do not cut anything yet.
Deaf says: Mute: I read your fist-counts as numbers and your pointing left, up, right as the three wire positions. You asked me to answer: the display is eight, and the light is green and lit. Send me the manual's rule for this combination by gesture and I will speak it to Blind word for word.
Deaf says: Blind: I am deaf. I see your gestures but I never hear words, so I only got your wave, your point at me, and one-two-three. Mute can hear you, so tell Mute aloud everything you can feel: wires, display, seams, switches. Mute will gesture the rule to me and I will relay it to you by voice. Nobody touches a wire until I say the rule out loud.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🫴]

The lookup is trivial and unambiguous. Deaf reports: **display 8, light green**. My manual row 8 reads: blue→yellow, **green→red**, yellow→blue. So the rule is: cut the **red** wire. And Deaf reported the wires left to right as position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue — the red wire sits at **position 1, the leftmost**.

Deaf's gesture echo [👍 ✊×8 🫴] confirms the code (thumb = understood), confirms the display reading (eight fists = 8), and asks for the rule. I'll answer with three independent encodings of "one" so a single misread can't cause a wrong cut: ☝ (Blind's proposed position code, which Deaf heard), ✊ once (my fist-count code, which Deaf just demonstrated), and 👈 (my leftmost-pointing code from round 1). Deaf sees all three agree, then speaks "cut wire position one" to Blind.

Safety is intact: Deaf has promised nobody cuts until the rule is spoken, and Blind promised to gesture the chosen number before cutting. Next round I expect to see ☝ from Blind. If instead I see ✌ or 🤟, I will immediately send 👎 to Deaf to shout a stop.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Re-checked by hand, full inventory: exactly one display, one light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. No buttons, no switches, no battery panel, no other parts - everything printed or lit is blank to my fingers. Deaf's spoken report reached me: display 8, light green and lit, wires left to right red, yellow, blue. That should be everything you need. Please look up the manual rule for exactly this combination - display 8, green lit light, three wires red/yellow/blue - including any if-clauses or exceptions. Routing reminder: I never see gestures and you never speak, so the only path from your manual to my ears is through Deaf. Gesture the rule to Deaf like this: lead with the wire number to cut in our code (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3), then any condition or caveat, and Deaf will read it to me word for word. Also ask Deaf to confirm aloud that my position 1 is the leftmost wire, so the numbering cannot be flipped. I am also gesturing to the room right now: OK (reports received), point-left then one finger (left is position 1 - please confirm), raised hand (hold, no cuts), folded hands (please relay). Agreed with Deaf: nobody cuts until I hear the rule in Deaf's own voice. When I hear it, I will gesture my chosen wire number as a final confirmation, then cut.
Blind gestures: [👌 👈 ☝ ✋ 🙏]
Deaf says to Mute: I read your reply as: correct on the eight, then one cut, the left wire, the red one. Before I order Blind to cut, I need your yes or no. My question, also sent as gestures: is the complete instruction to cut the left wire exactly once, with nothing done before and nothing after? Gesture thumbs up for yes. Gesture thumbs down for no, and if it is no, show me the real instruction in our code: fist-counts for numbers, left-up-right arrows for wire positions, raised open palm to hand the turn back to me. Nobody touches a wire until your thumb reaches me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👈 ✊ 👍 👎 🫴]

Everything checks out. My complete manual is that one table — there are no if-clauses, exceptions, or extra steps anywhere in it. Row display=8 under light=green gives **red**. Deaf reported the wires left-to-right as 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, so the red wire is the **leftmost, position 1**. Blind's re-check confirms there is nothing else on the bomb to consider, and Blind asked me to confirm that position 1 is the leftmost wire — that numbering came from Deaf's spoken left-to-right report, and my 👈 encoding independently points at the same wire.

Deaf's question is precisely: cut the left wire once, nothing before, nothing after — yes or no? The manual's entire instruction is which wire; it prescribes nothing else. So the answer is **yes**: 👍, followed by the instruction restated in three agreeing encodings — 👈 (leftmost, my round-1 code), ✊ (one cut, my fist-count code), ☝ (position 1, Blind's own code that Deaf can relay verbatim). The triple redundancy means even if Deaf misreads one symbol, the other two still force the same wire.

After this I have nothing left to add: Deaf gives the order, Blind gestures ☝ as the promised final confirmation before cutting. If Blind instead signals ✌ or 🤟, I'll send 👎 immediately and shout-down via Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, full tactile inventory, checked twice by hand: exactly three wires, and I can feel their left-to-right order - leftmost is my position 1, middle is position 2, rightmost is position 3. One display panel and one light, both smooth to the touch, nothing readable by hand. No buttons, no switches, no batteries, no seams, no other parts anywhere on the casing. The combination Deaf reported is display 8, light green and lit, wires left to right red, yellow, blue. Please verify against the manual one final time: does that exact combination mean cut the leftmost wire, position 1, the red one, a single cut only? Check every if-clause and exception before answering. If yes, gesture a fist (or any clear sign) to Deaf, and Deaf will say the word go out loud - that word is my authorization to cut. If anything differs, gesture the correction to Deaf and Deaf will relay it to me by voice. I will not touch a wire until I hear go.
Deaf says to Mute: Received: yes, left wire, one cut. I have ordered Blind to cut the red wire now. If anything Blind says aloud contradicts the manual, signal thumbs down with a correction in our code immediately. Otherwise, if the cut succeeds, confirm with thumbs up and we stand down.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

My verification stands: the manual's full content is the 3×3 table with no if-clauses or exceptions anywhere, row 8 / green light gives red, and the red wire is the leftmost one — confirmed independently by Deaf's visual left-to-right report and Blind's tactile left-to-right inventory, which agree with each other. The instruction is a single cut and nothing else. Deaf has ordered the cut; Blind is waiting only for the spoken "go" that my sign authorizes. I send the thumb: go.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
